The real-valued spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The negative-index branch defines, for example, both Y_{1,-1} and Y_{2,-1} as φ. Thus the family contains identical functions and is not orthonormal. Away from the coordinate seam, the displayed Laplacian applied to φ is zero, not −ℓ(ℓ+1)φ. Consequently the asserted eigenfunction identity and the subsequent diagonalization and Parseval arguments do not hold for the functions actually defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the entire negative-index branch by the normalized cosine partner of the positive-index sine branch, using |m| in the Legendre function and factorials.
issues.overall_effect: The solution representation, spectral construction, and estimates relying on an orthonormal Laplace eigenbasis are invalid under the supplied definition.
issues.title: The defined negative-index functions are not spherical eigenfunctions
issues.why_classification: A local standard correction of the basis specification restores the intended construction without changing any substantive approximation method or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $p\geq2$ and $L\in  L^p(\Omega,H^\eta(\S^2))$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:StrongLevyProcess}, where the processes $(L_{\ell,m})_{\ell,m}$ are assumed to be independent if $p>2$, and $\rho-\eta\leq1$;
\le C \left(\int_0^t \varlm e^{-2\ell(\ell+1)(t-s)} \diff s \right)^{p/2}

issues.failure_explanation: For jump martingales, the displayed deterministic quantity is the predictable bracket, not the random quadratic variation needed for this BDG estimate. Higher moments contain an additional jump-moment contribution. Independence across modes does not remove it. A counterexample is p=4, η=0, X⁰=0, and independent compensated Poisson coordinates L_{ℓ,0}(t)=N_ℓ(t)−ℓ^{-3}t, with all other coordinates zero. The total jump rate is finite and L has all finite moments in L². Nevertheless the fourth H¹ moment of its convolution contains contributions comparable to ∑ℓ^{-3}ℓ(ℓ+1), which diverges. Thus the claimed one-derivative L^p gain is false.

issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary estimate is false for backward Euler, leaving the cited initial-data smoothing arguments unsupported as written.
issues.title: The backward-Euler exponential error bound has an impossible decay factor

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem only permits β<α/2, so it does not supply the asserted O(h) endpoint at α=2. That endpoint can actually fail: take unit-rate Poisson components with a_ℓ=ℓ^{-1}, X⁰=0, backward Euler, and κ comparable to h^{-1/2}. The displayed exact and discrete variance formulas give a second-moment error at least c h∑_{ℓ≤κ}(2ℓ+1)ℓ^{-2}, hence c h log κ. For uncentered Poisson noise the mean-square contribution has the same sign and cannot cancel this lower bound.
